_note: goals-decomposer's checked-in routing corpus. LEXICAL-OVERLAP legibility aid, NOT a verdict — routing-eval.py measures token overlap between a phrase and the description only. Positives span the invocation families (imperative 'grade/decompose this PRD/charter', diagnostic 'are these goals measurable / ranked / governable', symptom 'no metric / all P0 / works-well acceptance / outputs-not-outcomes / surrogate metric', the CROSS-CHECK family 'goals vs the architecture', plus 2-3 paraphrases). Negatives are drawn ADVERSARIALLY from the CONFUSABLE neighbours: product-forge (judges the product BET by expert taste — this skill grades the charter's GOVERNABILITY, not the bet's merit), architecture-decomposer (the INSIDE-OUT structure that MEETS the goals), and the other code decomposers (code/type/query). Each negative belongs to a NAMED peer. Re-derive when the neighbourhood changes.
positives: are these project goals measurable or just fluff
is this charter a strict priority order or is everything P0
decompose these goals into a falsifiable charter
this goal has no metric or threshold — is it a real goal
rank the architecture characteristics (the -ilities) for this system
does this KPI actually capture the outcome or is it a surrogate (Goodhart)
the acceptance criteria say 'works well and feels snappy' — make them checkable
is there a diagnosis behind these goals or just a wish list
cross-check these ranked goals against the proposed architecture
write success criteria for this project so we can tell when it's done
this PRD is all outputs (ship X, build Y), not outcomes
grade the OUTSIDE-IN goals doc on aim and measurability
are these non-goals explicit or is the scope unbounded
negatives: is this product bet a good idea, what would Marty C. say
run the product council on this strategy and roadmap
design the system architecture and module boundaries
grade this dependency graph for cycles, layering, and coupling
decompose and grade this function against its contract
make illegal states unrepresentable in this data model
grade this SQL query's grain and execution plan
is this brand-guidelines spec operable and traced
review this code for the green-but-wrong quadrant
design the bounded contexts and ownership for these services
